transcript: January in New York, of course, is festival season. Here are all of the festival shows that I saw in week two of being in New York. Starting off with maybe one of the weirdest pieces of theater I've seen is Anne live Young's Marie and Twinette. I honestly don't even know how to describe this show. Don't even know what it's about. I'm still processing the show a week later. This show was intense and obscene and borderline offensive, and I also got hit with a pile of dough, but I, I, I think I enjoyed it. I was thoroughly entertained from start to finish by not just what was happening on stage, but the audience around me. I felt a lot of feelings, and I've been thinking about it ever since, but I could not tell you what the show is about. And sometimes I love that in theater. Next up, I saw The Seventh Voyage of Egon Tishy, which is a piece of science fiction about this guy trapped in space who gets sucked into a time loop. His entire show originally started digitally, and you can still feel that in the way that it's being presented live. Similarly to if you saw the original live stream of Circle Jerk, and then when they performed Circle Jerk in a theater. Entire show is performed by one actor in this box who's being filmed the entire time and projected on screens on either side of the box. And his live Performance is being overlaid with some pre recorded bits, and the way that it is spliced together in real time is, like, really freaking cool. Overall, this was just really cool to watch be performed live. And it's science fiction, and, you know, I'm a fan of science fiction. Because of the looping nature of the story, there were times where it became a little frustrating to watch, in the same way that I get frustrated watching, like, Wile E. Coyote Road Runner cartoon, if you know what I mean. But ultimately, I think this show really sticks the landing in a way that I feel justify some of that frustration I felt along the way to get there. And again, the staging is just so freaking cool. And finally, I saw Night Side Songs, which is the newest musical by the Lazoors, which I thought was going to be a song cycle, but it felt much more like a full structured musical. Night Side Songs is a musical that cycles through different stages of having cancer, from symptoms all the way to death. That primarily focuses on one central female character, but between her scenes, it's also interspersed with, like, other characters throughout time. But the most unique aspect of this musical was how communal it was. This is not a program. This is a song book that they give you at the beginning of the show, featuring all of the lyrics that you are going to sing along. With them throughout the show. There were five fantastic performers in the show, uh, who played multiple characters. But Taylor Trench also kind of was, like, the designated choir director, and so anytime that he would come on, he would, like, teach you the parts that you were going to sing in a song as they started the song, and then, like, everybody else would join in. And it was just. It was really freaking cool. And I thought that was such a cool approach to this material, because illness can feel very isolating, but knowing that everyone around you is still supporting you as you are going through the songs and that you're not alone. There were times where I would start choking up because of what was happening in the show itself, and I couldn't get a line that I was supposed to be singing out at the time. But you could still hear everybody around you singing it. And even if you, like, did not feel comfortable singing, everybody around you was still supporting you, which, in the context of the show, just works so well for me. It's music by the lazuurs, and I. I freaking love their music. If you haven't listened to their EPs online, definitely do that. I love their music, and we live in Cairo. I loved their music here. Out of all the shows that I saw under the radar this year, Nightside Songs is hands down my favorite. And I Think the overall the writing needs a little reworking, but I really love this concept, and I'm excited to see what happens with the show in the future.
